slides.title: A page on your computer
slides.html: The ODMDM connector runs on your computer and opens as a page in the browser. It talks to your MDM with your token, never to Deploy App.

slides.title: Get it from Deploy App
slides.html: In Deploy App, as an admin, open User Management, then MDM. Press Install the ODMDM connector.

slides.title: No such button?
slides.html: A Deploy App that does not offer the download has no such button. Then see Install the connector from a terminal.

slides.title: Download it
slides.html: Press Download for Windows, or your system's: on an Intel Mac, choose macOS (Intel) under Other systems first. If your browser holds the download, choose to keep the file.

slides.title: Is it the released file?
slides.html: Before you open it: the dialog shows the file's SHA-256 and version. To be sure, download SHA256SUMS from that version's release under github.com/pvarki/python-odmdm-fleet/releases and compare your file's line.

slides.title: Check the file itself
slides.html: Technical staff can check the downloaded file itself: in its folder, these lines print its SHA-256, which must be the dialog's; capitals do not matter. On a Mac it checks the .zip, before it is unzipped.

slides.title: On Windows
slides.html: Open the downloaded file. If Windows stops it with Windows protected your PC, choose More info, then Run anyway.

slides.title: Windows will not run it?
slides.html: If Windows offers no Run anyway, this computer does not run unsigned files. Ask whoever runs it, or use another computer.

slides.title: On a Mac
slides.html: Open odmdm-connector from your downloads; unzip it first if needed. On an Intel Mac, it is the file for macOS (Intel).

slides.title: When macOS stops it
slides.html: The first time, macOS stops it with a warning like this one. Press Done, not Move to Trash.

slides.title: Open Anyway
slides.html: Open System Settings, Privacy & Security, scroll down and press Open Anyway, there for about an hour. Enter your login password and press OK, then Open when the warning comes back.

slides.title: On Linux
slides.html: Download the file for Linux and unpack it. Then, in its folder, run ./odmdm-connector in a terminal.

slides.title: Keep its window open
slides.html: The connector opens a window (on Linux, it is your terminal) and runs while it is open. If the page did not open, open the address the window shows.

slides.title: It opens in your browser
slides.html: The connector's page opens in your default browser: use Deploy App in that same browser. The first time it asks you to add your Deploy App: see Connect your MDM.

slides.title: Next time
slides.html: Next time, open the same file again and use the page it opens. Every start makes a new address, and a page left open from before asks for it.

slides.title: What it keeps
slides.html: With Remember on this computer ticked, your token goes to the computer's keychain, never to a file. The challenge is held only while the connector runs.

slides.title: Upgrade it
slides.html: The dialog shows the version your Deploy App offers. For a newer one, stop the connector, download it again, check it as before and use the new file: your settings stay.

slides.title: Remove it
slides.html: First open the Deploy App's name at the top right and remove each Deploy App, so the keychain keeps no token. Then stop the connector and delete the file.
